routes.reason: The Part II MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII, 39 items. The frontier is right: MordellLawrenceVenkatesh's LV.0–LV.11 plan the Lawrence–Venkatesh method for curves — Faltings's finiteness lemma, abelian-by-finite families, the complex and p-adic period maps, crystalline comparison on residue disks — and this paper runs the same three-realization argument with coefficients in a rank-one local system, with a possibly disconnected reductive group, and with a monodromy group known only to be strongly c-balanced. Every layer here strengthens a layer there, so a new roadmap would duplicate LV.1–LV.11, and the generalizations are not statements those layers plan, so a source route would misfile them; the route's reason says both, and I agree. The brief states the final theorems exactly — Theorem 8.17 with its two Hodge-number inequalities, the p-adic Bakker–Tsimerman theorem 6.4, Faltings's finiteness lemma for disconnected groups (Lemma 5.49) and the three Diophantine cases (dim A ≥ 4; dim A = 3 under the d(i) divisibility hypothesis; dim A = 2 from the curve case) — and lists the layers to cover. Worth flagging to the orchestrator, not against the route: its parent is a **draft** roadmap (research/blueprint/roadmaps/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json, status draft), the only such Part II in the whole paper corpus — 75 of the other 76 non-atlas parents are Tau Ceti roadmaps. So this Part II's design job has to be sequenced after its parent's, and no other parent would be defensible.

The new roadmap SheafConvolutionOnAbelianVarieties, 26 items. I checked the three exclusions the reason gives and all three hold: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5 plans the perverse t-structure and intermediate extensions but says nothing about convolution, the quotient by negligible sheaves or a convolution monodromy group; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.6 is a different Tannakian category (motivic Galois groups); and GeometricSatakeAndFusion's convolution is on affine Grassmannians, a different geometry. The theory is Krämer–Weissauer's, self-contained and with its own applications, and separating it means the Part II can import one statement (Corollary 4.10) instead of re-planning perverse sheaves. The brief states the convolution category, the arithmetic–geometric exact sequence, Theorem 3.5 (with its SL_N/Sp_N/SO_N trichotomy and N = (−1)^{n−1}[H]^n), Theorem 4.7 with Corollary 4.10 and Proposition 4.11. Keeping the Eulerian-number combinatorics of Appendices B–C here is right, since it exists only to eliminate the exceptional Tannakian groups.

LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.6, 1 item (o-minimality and Ax–Schanuel-type transcendence for period maps). LD.6 is titled 'o-minimality, definable counting and unlikely intersections' and plans exactly the o-minimal structures, definable sets and transcendence statements this item names; nothing about it is specific to this paper.
SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0, 1 item. A foundational scheme-theoretic statement that belongs with the foundations layer, not with either new roadmap.
ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2, 2 items. Elementary arithmetic inputs that CA.2 owns; routing them to the Part II would have buried elementary material inside a Hodge-theoretic roadmap.

notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-7b31c4 (review job issue #1068). I fetched arXiv 2004.09046v5 myself; its SHA-256 is 5e5f829e2841637de38852bde0d5f0a0b80183e6f9d23b60250cc2be1ee21d97, matching the hash the extraction records. Verdict: accept, after two corrections made in place. (1) The one library item cited mathlib:Nat.succ_mul_choose_eq, which does not exist at Mathlib 082e2d3 — the name has no occurrence anywhere in the pinned tree, because it is the pre-rename form. The lemma is Nat.add_one_mul_choose_eq, '(n + 1) * choose n k = choose (n + 1) (k + 1) * (k + 1)', at Mathlib/Data/Nat/Choose/Basic.lean:131; the citation is corrected and the note records why. The item's other three declarations (Nat.choose, Nat.factorial, Nat.choose_symm) are all present. (2) Item 72's note said only that the Tau Ceti Hodge structures roadmap is existing work. It now records what is actually built — TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructure and HodgeStructureOn, MixedHodgeStructure with its weight filtration (215 declarations), Polarization with the Hodge form (61) and PeriodDomain.Point — and what is not: there is no variation of Hodge structure and no Griffiths transversality in either library, which is precisely the part this paper varies. The status stays planned. Item 73 already made the same distinction for abelian varieties, accurately, which is the standard the amended note now meets. Everything else holds. All 69 missing items are routed exactly once; the 12 planned items all cite layers that plan them, and I read each layer's description (EDC.5/EDC.1 for perverse sheaves, MC.6 and Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 1 for Tannakian groups, LV.1/LV.3/LV.4 for the Lawrence–Venkatesh inputs, Tau Ceti HodgeStructures L0/L1/L3, A2 for abelian schemes, R28.5 and RP.4 for Shafarevich, SF.5 for Riemann–Roch, LD.6 for o-minimality, Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layers 6–8 with RG2.0, WC.3 and DWP.7 for the Weil conjectures, R09.7 for resolution). No missing item is in either library: searches for perverse sheaves, Tannakian categories, period maps, Néron–Severi groups, Eulerian numbers, crystalline comparison, Shafarevich finiteness and Bakker–Tsimerman all return nothing. A sweep of the paper's own numbering found no statement on the way to the main theorems without an item: of 196 paper-internal numbered statements, every one is covered once the items' ranges ('Lemmas B.19 through B.31' and the like) are expanded, and the eleven apparent gaps are all citations of other papers ([47, Theorem 1.4], [37, Corollary 7.4], [48, Lemma 2.12], …) or Proposition B.1, which the paper itself labels '(Proposition 3.15)' and item 20 covers. The extraction records no sourceIssues. I checked the main theorems and their arithmetic — the recursion a(1)=1, a(2)=5, a(i+2)=4a(i+1)+1−a(i) and d(i)=C(a(i)+a(i+1),a(i)) give exactly the paper's d(1)=6, d(2)=53130, d(3)=216182590635135019896 and d(4)≈2.5×10^79, which I verified by exact computation, and item 3 states them correctly — and found nothing to record. I did not read all 121 pages hunting for mistakes, and record none. python3 scripts/check_paper.py reports ok.
